name: GestorVet
tagline: Spanish-language practice management software for veterinary clinics: client and animal records, visits, appointments, and billing in one portal.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The visible part of this, clients, animals, visits, vaccination reminders, invoices, is textbook CRUD and an agent will produce something usable in an afternoon. The part that actually matters in a clinic is everything around it: prescription and antibiotic-use reporting to the national registry, microchip registry submissions, legally compliant electronic invoicing and tax rules, lab analyzer and imaging integrations, and a decade of animal history that nobody is re-typing. A practice also cannot run on a build with no support number when the front desk cannot print an invoice on a Saturday morning. This is business software with regulators attached, not a personal tool with a subscription, so a one-shot replacement is the wrong shape of solution. Build the CRUD version if you want to understand the domain, not if you want to stop paying.
coreLoopDIY: A local records app where you register clients and their animals, log visits with notes and weight, set vaccination reminders, and print a simple invoice.
requirements: a machine that stays on and gets backed up
someone willing to be tech support for the front desk
a separate, legally compliant path for invoicing and prescription reporting
whatYouLose: Prescription and antibiotic-use reporting to the veterinary registries, which is a legal obligation, not a feature
Compliant electronic invoicing and the tax plumbing that goes with it
Lab analyzer, imaging, and microchip registry integrations
Years of existing animal histories, unless you write and validate a migration
Somebody to call when the clinic is full and the software is not working
moatNotes: Veterinary software in Spain lives or dies on staying current with prescription reporting and invoicing rules. That is maintenance work forever, not a build.
whyPeopleStillPay: Clinics pay for the boring guarantee that the software will keep matching the law next year and that someone else is responsible when it does not. The records screens are commodity; the reporting pipelines, the analyzer drivers, the invoicing certification and the phone support are what the fee buys. Add the fact that all the clinic's history already lives inside it and that staff are trained on it, and the cost of leaving is much higher than the subscription.
notes: The animal records app is a weekend; the regulatory surface is not. The moat is prescription and invoicing compliance that has to be re-earned every time the rules change.
prompt:
Build a local-first veterinary clinic records app for a single small practice. Stack: Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLite via SQLModel, server-rendered Jinja2 templates with HTMX for partial updates, plain CSS. No React, no cloud services, no telemetry, no accounts system beyond one shared local password read from .env.

Data model: Client (name, phone, email, address, notes), Animal (belongs to Client: name, species, breed, sex, birth date, microchip number, neutered flag, notes), Visit (belongs to Animal: datetime, reason, exam notes, weight in kg, treatment given, price), Vaccination (belongs to Animal: vaccine name, date given, next due date), Appointment (optional Animal link, datetime, duration minutes, reason, status).

Screens:
1. Search bar at top of every page that matches clients by name or phone and animals by name or microchip.
2. Client page listing their animals and recent invoices.
3. Animal page: identity block, full visit history newest first, weight chart as a simple inline SVG, vaccination list with overdue rows highlighted.
4. New visit form on the animal page, submits over HTMX and appends to the history without a full reload.
5. Day view agenda for appointments with previous and next day links, plus a week view.
6. Dashboard: today's appointments, vaccinations due in the next 30 days, animals not seen in over 12 months.
7. Invoice view for a visit or a set of visits, rendered as a clean printable HTML page with line items, subtotal, configurable tax rate from .env, and total. Print via the browser only.

Also include: a CSV import command for clients and animals, a one-click database backup endpoint that copies the SQLite file to a dated file in ./backups, and seed data for about 20 clients and 30 animals so the UI is not empty on first run.

Explicitly out of scope, and say so in the README: prescription or antibiotic-use reporting to any national registry, certified electronic invoicing, microchip registry submission, lab analyzer or imaging integrations, payment processing, SMS or email sending, multi-clinic support, and any user roles or permissions.

Ship a README with setup in four commands, a .env.example containing APP_PASSWORD and TAX_RATE, and a short section stating that this app is not a legal record for prescription or invoicing purposes.
